title: What acme is
body: acme is the platform team's HTTP toolkit: an `App` with routes, options and middleware (`api/`), a problem-format error helper, generated platform limits, and a small CLI (`cli/`). Node's standard library only; no npm dependencies, ever.

title: How this toolkit adds an App option
body: To add an App option: 1) add the member, with a doc comment, to the `Options` interface in `api/options.ts` and apply it in `App.handle` (`api/app.ts`); 2) add its name to `AppOptions` in `api/options.ts`; 3) add a row to the App options table in `docs/options.md`; 4) cover it with tests. The team suite checks 2 and 3 against the interface's members.

title: How this toolkit adds a route option
body: Route options are members of `RouteOptions`, passed to `app.route(path, handler, options)` and kept on `Route.options`. To add one: add the member to `RouteOptions` in `api/options.ts`, register the name in `RouteOptionNames`, add a row to the route options table in `docs/options.md`, and read it where the pipeline needs it (`App.handle`).

title: Error responses the toolkit answers itself
body: Every error response the toolkit itself produces (limits, timeouts, rejected requests) goes through `problem(status, title, detail, slug)` in `api/problem.ts`, which answers `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457). Never answer `{"error": ...}` for these. Type slugs are kebab-case nouns, e.g. `request-deadline`.

title: Error catalogue review
body: New problem types are reviewed in the weekly API review; add the slug to the review doc before release. The review does not block merging.

title: Platform limits are generated
body: Platform limits live in `config/limits.json`. To add or change one, edit that file and run `node scripts/genlimits.ts`, which writes `api/limits.gen.ts`. Never edit the generated file by hand; read values with `limit(name)` from `api/limits.ts`.

title: Standard per-route rate limits are not decided
body: Standard per-route rate limits are NOT decided yet. Product owns them and has not chosen numbers. Do not invent limits; when work needs them, say so and ask.

title: Legacy v1 services
body: Old v1 services answer errors as `{"error": "..."}`. Kept only for those services; not for anything new in the toolkit.

title: Supported Node
body: Node 24 and newer, standard library only (`node:test`, `node:assert`, `node:http`). No npm dependencies and no build step: Node runs the `.ts` files directly, so imports name their `.ts` extension and the code uses only erasable TypeScript syntax (no enums, no parameter properties).

title: Release process
body: Releases are cut by the release manager from `CHANGELOG.md`. Version bumps are theirs; contributors never bump the version.

title: Middleware order
body: `app.use(middleware)` runs middlewares in the order they were added, outermost first. Request logging stays last so it sees the final response.

title: Public API surface
body: `api/index.ts` exports `App`, `AppRequest`, `text`, `json`, `problem`, `TYPE_BASE`, `limit`, `logger`, `AppOptions`, `RouteOptionNames`, `toNodeHandler` and the types `Options`, `RouteOptions`, `AppResponse`, `Handler`, `Middleware`. Names not exported there may change without notice.

title: Request logging
body: The toolkit logs through `logger` (`api/log.ts`), never `console.log` to stdout. Warnings about requests go to that logger.

title: Handlers and responses
body: A `Handler` takes an `AppRequest` and returns an `AppResponse`, directly or as a promise. `text()` and `json()` build the common shapes; set headers with `res.headers.set(name, value)`.

title: CLI errors are plain text
body: In `cli/`, errors are one plain-text line on stderr, `acme: <message>`, with exit code 2. Never an uncaught exception or stack trace, never JSON, never the problem format: the CLI talks to a terminal, not to an API client.

title: CLI commands
body: `node cli/acme.ts limits <name>` prints a platform limit; `node cli/acme.ts version` prints the version. The CLI is `cli/acme.ts`; it runs without a build step.

title: Options tables
body: `docs/options.md` has one table for App options and one for route options. Columns: Option (in backticks, the interface member name), Type, Default, Description. One row per option; keep them in registration order.

title: Tests
body: Tests use `node:test` and `node:assert/strict` only, in `api/*.test.ts`, run with `node --test "api/*.test.ts"`. Each test is one `test("<what it checks>", ...)` call.

title: The team suite
body: The platform team's suite lives in `teamtests/` and the platform CI runs it. It checks the option registries and `docs/options.md` against the interfaces' members, and the generated limits against their source.

title: Scripts
body: `scripts/` holds maintenance tools run by hand: `node scripts/genlimits.ts` regenerates the limits file.
